root_cause.text: In `rxgk_extract_token()` in `net/rxrpc/rxgk_app.c`, the ticket-length validation rounded up the untrusted `ticket_len` with `xdr_round_up()`, and that rounding operation could overflow before the bounds check was performed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container))` to `if (ticket_len > xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container)))`, and the commit message explicitly says the fix is to avoid “rounding up the value to be tested (which might overflow)” by rounding down the available data instead.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `rxgk_extract_token()` in `net/rxrpc/rxgk_app.c`, the ticket-length validation rounded up the untrusted `ticket_len` with `xdr_round_up()`, and that rounding operation could overflow before the bounds check was performed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container))` to `if (ticket_len > xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container)))`, and the commit message explicitly says the fix is to avoid “rounding up the value to be tested (which might overflow)” by rounding down the available data instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix token length validation to use the correct XDR rounding direction when checking for short packets.
intent_record.what: The packet-length validation in `rxgk_extract_token()` was changed from checking whether `xdr_round_up(ticket_len)` exceeds `token_len - sizeof(container)` to checking whether `ticket_len` exceeds `xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container))`.
intent_record.how: This alters the bounds check for extracting the token ticket so that the code now validates the unrounded ticket length against the available payload after rounding the container-adjusted length down, which can prevent rejecting valid packets or accepting improperly sized ones due to mismatched XDR rounding semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an XDR alignment helper for rounding values down to a 32-bit boundary.
intent_record.what: A new macro definition was added: `xdr_round_down(x)` expands to `round_down((x), sizeof(__be32))`, placed alongside the existing `xdr_round_up(x)` macro. No existing code was modified.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable helper for aligning a length down to the nearest 32-bit XDR boundary. At runtime, it enables code elsewhere in the file to compute truncated XDR-aligned sizes consistently instead of duplicating the rounding logic.

grouping_result.intent: Fix token length validation to use the correct XDR rounding direction when checking for short packets.
Add an XDR alignment helper for rounding values down to a 32-bit boundary.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s intent matches the root cause: it fixes token/ticket length validation in rxgk_extract_token() and specifically addresses incorrect XDR rounding during bounds checking, which is the flaw that allowed overflow before validation.

The change adds a helper for rounding values down to a 32-bit boundary, while the vulnerability was caused by unsafe rounding up of an untrusted ticket length before bounds checking in rxgk_extract_token(). This does not address that overflow issue.

candidates.rationale: This is the vulnerable bounds check: it rounds up the untrusted ticket_len before comparing it, so the rounding can overflow before the validation occurs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the vulnerable bounds check in rxgk_extract_token(): it applies xdr_round_up() to the untrusted ticket_len before validating it against the available token size, so the rounding can overflow prior to the check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the vulnerable logic and the added mitigation. The root cause was in `rxgk_extract_token()` where an untrusted length was validated with `xdr_round_up(ticket_len)` before a bounds check, which could overflow. The old check is still visible in the diff context: `if (xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - 3 * 4)` and the commit changes it to first precheck `if (token_len < sizeof(container)) goto short_packet;` and then use `if (xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container)) goto short_packet;`. This means the vulnerable construct was present before the fix, but in this commit the code already contains the correct precheck and safer handling, so the fix is present.
